Sizes that reach a target informativeness

Source: R/design.R
solve_design.Rd

Computes, for a balanced design, the site size needed for a target informativeness with a given number of sites, or the largest number of sites that reaches the target with a given total.

Usage

solve_design(target_I, sigma_tau, kappa, J = NULL, N = NULL)

Arguments

target_I

Target informativeness, a number strictly between 0 and 1.

sigma_tau

Planned between-site standard deviation, a positive number, or a numeric vector of them for a range of scenarios.

kappa

Constant \(\kappa\) of the sampling variances \(v_j = \kappa / n_j\), a positive number (see neyman_variance()).

J, N

The number of sites or the total number of individuals: give one of them.

Value

A data frame with one row per value of sigma_tau and the columns

  • target_I, sigma_tau, kappa: the inputs.

  • J, n_per_site, N: the design, with n_per_site not rounded.

  • I, with N given: the informativeness reached with the number of sites rounded down. J, n_per_site and I are NA when the total cannot reach the target even in a single site.

Details

Under balance \(I = \sigma_\tau^2 / (\sigma_\tau^2 + \kappa / \bar n)\), so the target needs \(\bar n = (\kappa / \sigma_\tau^2)\, I/(1 - I)\) individuals per site, and with a total \(N\) at most \(J = N \sigma_\tau^2 (1 - I) / (\kappa I)\) sites, rounded down. Under balance the informativeness depends on the size per site, not on the number of sites: with J given, the target fixes the size per site, and with N given, it fixes how many sites the total can be divided into. Because sigma_tau is unknown at the planning stage, a vector of plausible values gives one row per scenario.

At a fixed total, more sites lower the informativeness but make the mean effect more precise: its variance under balance is \(\sigma_\tau^2/J + \kappa/N\) (Appendix E.3). The two are different design questions.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

reliability_design() and plot_design(), and vignette("planning").

Examples

solve_design(target_I = 0.5, sigma_tau = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3), kappa = 4, J = 40)
#>   target_I sigma_tau kappa  J n_per_site         N
#> 1      0.5       0.1     4 40  400.00000 16000.000
#> 2      0.5       0.2     4 40  100.00000  4000.000
#> 3      0.5       0.3     4 40   44.44444  1777.778
solve_design(target_I = 0.5, sigma_tau = 0.2, kappa = 4, N = 4000)
#>   target_I sigma_tau kappa  J n_per_site    N   I
#> 1      0.5       0.2     4 40        100 4000 0.5
